title: Domestic intellectual property rights protection and the margins of bilateral exports
summary: Earlier research on domestic intellectual property rights (IPR) protection and trade has looked mostly at imports. This paper turns to exports and finds that IPRs are trade-related and can help boost exports in both developed and developing countries.
keyFindings: Stronger IPR protection can boost exports in both developed and developing countries.
IPR strength in the exporting country matters more than in the importing country.
The effect works mainly through the extensive margin; effects on the intensive margin are mostly insignificant.
